scenes.paragraphMeaning: The chapter opens on a late-July afternoon beside the old canal in Funaki, where the family’s calligraphy school and its wooden sign stand among traditional tiled-roof homes.
scenes.sceneDescription: A quiet establishing view of the Japanese canal town Funaki: tied wooden boats, dark tiled-roof houses and the Takagi calligraphy school with a simple blank wooden signboard, in warm late-July afternoon light.
scenes.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: first of three inline landscape paintings for Kanji Trail, The “Closed” Sign, chapter 1; place after paragraph 0.
Input images: Images 1–3 are approved Kasa Jizō inline-style references only. Image 4 guides Mio’s character identity and palette only; do not copy its interior composition or pose.
Scene/backdrop: the invented Japanese canal town of Funaki on a warm late-July afternoon. A narrow old canal runs past small wooden boats tied along the bank and traditional wooden houses with dark kawara tile roofs. One house is the Takagi calligraphy school.
Subject/action: quiet exterior establishing view, with the canal and school as the focal setting. A single plain wooden signboard hangs beside the school entrance, but its face is entirely blank. No people are needed.
Style/medium: simple painted children’s picture-book art matching the approved Kasa Jizō inline treatment: broad smooth colour areas, gentle contours, minimal surface texture, few purposeful shadows, a quiet simplified background and two or three depth layers; substantially simpler than cover art.
Composition/framing: full-bleed 12:7 landscape; use a clear canal-side perspective with the school among the houses, readable at small size.
Lighting/mood: soft warm afternoon daylight, calm and slightly wistful.
Palette: warm ivory walls and paper, muted teal canal water, sage willow leaves, restrained ochre wood and dark indigo roof shadows.
Constraints: match paragraph 0 only. Treat Funaki as a Japanese town; use Japanese wooden architecture, tiled roofs and small moored boats.
Avoid: any legible writing, kanji, letters, numbers, calligraphy strokes, signs with marks, modern cars, western houses, crowds, logos, borders, watermarks, photorealism, glossy 3D, dense textures, intricate brushwork or cover-level detail.

scenes.paragraphMeaning: Mio removes the “Closed Today” sign from the classroom door; a white envelope drops to her feet, carrying her grandfather’s first clue.
scenes.sceneDescription: Inside the quiet tatami calligraphy school, Mio lifts a completely blank wooden sign from its hook as a small white envelope lies freshly fallen on the floor beside her; the envelope and sign have no writing.
scenes.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: second of three inline landscape paintings for Kanji Trail, The “Closed” Sign, chapter 1; place after paragraph 5.
Input images: Images 1–3 are approved Kasa Jizō inline-style references only. Image 4 guides Mio’s character identity and muted palette only; do not copy its pose, window framing or composition.
Scene/backdrop: a modest Japanese calligraphy classroom with tatami, a wooden doorframe and a few ink brushes and inkstones set back quietly in the room. Keep the room simple, uncluttered and recognisably Japanese.
Subject/action: twelve-year-old Mio, a Japanese girl with black hair tied in a low ponytail, an ivory short-sleeved shirt and a muted sage-green skirt, has just lifted a plain wooden placard from a small hook on the classroom door. A small white envelope has fallen onto the tatami by her feet. She looks down at it with surprise and uncertainty. The placard and envelope are completely blank.
Character continuity: use Image 4 only for Mio’s face, hairstyle and ivory-and-sage palette; her clothes are simple everyday clothes, with no backpack in this indoor moment.
Style/medium: simple painted children’s picture-book art matching the approved Kasa Jizō inline treatment: broad smooth colour areas, gentle contours, minimal surface texture, few purposeful folds and shadows, a quiet simplified background and two or three depth layers; simpler than cover art.
Composition/framing: full-bleed 12:7 landscape; show Mio, the small empty hook and the envelope together as clear focal shapes, with ample quiet room around them.
Lighting/mood: gentle afternoon light, intimate and mysterious but not frightening.
Palette: warm ivory tatami and paper, soft wood ochre, muted teal shadows and sage-green clothing.
Constraints: match paragraph 5 only. No other people; preserve the discovery without revealing what the letter says.
Avoid: visible writing, kanji, letters, numbers, calligraphy marks, text on the sign or envelope, extra figures, logos, borders, watermarks, photorealism, glossy 3D, dense texture, busy props or cover-level detail.

scenes.paragraphMeaning: At night Mio discovers the classroom drawers emptied and blank papers scattered; a face-hidden figure with a black umbrella slips through the garden gate.
scenes.sceneDescription: Mio stands in the dark classroom beside an open desk with seven pulled-out drawers and blank sheets scattered across tatami, looking through the garden-facing glass door at a face-hidden black-umbrella silhouette leaving through the gate into night.
scenes.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: third of three inline landscape paintings for Kanji Trail, The “Closed” Sign, chapter 1; place after paragraph 13.
Input images: Images 1–3 are approved Kasa Jizō inline-style references only. Image 4 guides Mio’s character identity and palette only; do not copy its bright daytime interior composition.
Scene/backdrop: the Takagi family’s Japanese calligraphy school at night. Inside is a dark, quiet tatami classroom; beyond the garden-facing glass sliding door are a small garden and a narrow wooden gate opening onto the night.
Subject/action: Mio, a twelve-year-old Japanese girl with black hair tied in a low ponytail, ivory shirt and muted sage-green skirt, stands inside holding still in alarm. Her grandfather’s low desk has its seven drawers pulled open and plain, completely blank sheets lie scattered over the tatami. Outside, a single distant figure carrying a black umbrella is just passing through the garden gate into darkness. Show only a silhouette from behind; the face and identity remain hidden.
Character continuity: use Image 4 only for Mio’s face, low ponytail and ivory-and-sage palette. Keep her recognisable but small in the scene.
Style/medium: simple painted children’s picture-book art matching the approved Kasa Jizō inline treatment: broad smooth colour areas, gentle contours, minimal surface texture, few purposeful shadows, a quiet simplified background and two or three depth layers; much simpler than cover art.
Composition/framing: full-bleed 12:7 landscape; the open drawers and scattered blank papers are visible in the foreground, Mio near the doorway, and the anonymous umbrella figure small beyond the glass.
Lighting/mood: cool midnight indigo with a restrained warm interior glow; suspenseful but gentle, not horror.
Palette: midnight indigo, warm ivory papers, muted teal glass shadows, soft ochre wood and a small amount of sage.
Constraints: match paragraph 13 only. Keep the stranger anonymous and the mystery unresolved; the umbrella is the only identifying feature. All papers are blank.
Avoid: any visible face or identity, violence, weapon, text, kanji, letters, numbers, legible calligraphy, marks on paper, logos, borders, watermarks, horror imagery, photorealism, glossy 3D, dense detail or cover-level texture.
